title: The Light of Asia
hookLine: Edwin Arnold's long poem of the Buddha's life, told in English verse
carry: a dewdrop slipping into the shining sea

lines: FROM THE DESK TO THE PARLOR.
A WHOLE LIFE AS A POEM.
cards: What happens when the Buddha's story leaves the scholar's desk and lands in a parlor? A translation of the Dhammapada is careful, scholarly work.
But an English poet and newspaperman named Edwin Arnold had a different idea.
He would tell the whole life of the Buddha as a long poem: the palace, the four sights, the night he left, the tree, the awakening, the teaching. In English verse, for ordinary readers.

teach.h: AN ORIGINAL POEM, NOT A SCRIPTURE.
teach.b: The Light of Asia is not a translation of any one scripture. It's an original English poem, in long, rolling lines, drawing on the traditional stories of the Buddha's life.

Its subtitle calls it The Great Renunciation, and Arnold presents it as told by an Indian Buddhist, so the voice is meant to be a believer's, speaking with love. The story is one this path has told already.
The young prince Siddhartha grows up in a palace where sorrow is hidden from him. He sees age, sickness, death, and a wandering holy man.

teach.h: THE PRINCE, THE NIGHT, THE TREE.
teach.b: He leaves his sleeping wife and child in the night, searches, nearly starves, sits beneath the tree, and wakes up. Then he teaches. The poem tells it with color: gardens, music, horses, moonlight.

teach.h: A DEWDROP SLIPS INTO THE SEA.
teach.b: Near the end, after the teaching of nirvana, Arnold leaves a picture: a dewdrop slipping into the shining sea.

teach.h: INTO HOMES THE SCHOLARS NEVER REACHED.
teach.b: A small, bright thing letting go of its edges and becoming part of something vast. Readers have argued about whether that's what nirvana means, and Buddhist teachers explain it in different ways.
But the picture stayed with people.
For some readers in Britain and America, this poem was their first meeting with the Buddha at all, not as a curiosity but as a teacher worth loving.
It's long and old-fashioned, and critics have called it more Victorian than Indian in places. Still, it carried the story into homes the scholars never reached.

how: The Light of Asia is no longer a scripture anyone practices from, but it is still read as literature, and some Western Buddhists and readers of Buddhism remember it as the book that first introduced them to the Buddha's life.

games.q: you're Edwin Arnold. the scholars have careful translations. you want ordinary families to meet the Buddha. what do you write?
o: a long poem of his whole life, for ordinary readers.
games.why: he wrote The Light of Asia, the Buddha's life in English verse, told in the voice of an Indian Buddhist.

practice: Take Arnold's last picture, a single dewdrop, bright on a leaf, and on each out-breath let it slip a little closer to the water. You don't need to decide what it means. Just let the small thing rest in the large one.
